=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Draft (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Headline:** The seller's package shifts almost all known risk to the buyer. Four quantified known items total **AUD 4,130,000** (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 420k, Sandbar 330k, Ironquay 180k). That is close to the seller's entire AUD 4.8m general cap, and the buyer-knowledge and data-room disclosure clauses would bar claims on those same items. The seller's "FINAL / market / not to be re-opened" language is advocacy, not a binding agreement. I have not verified its market claims, and the deal team should confirm whether any principal-level agreement was actually signed.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** General cap at 50% of price as an opening position, with a floor of about 30%. Fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50%. The cap should not be the only protection on known issues, which are already quantified above.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Claims under AUD 25,000 are excluded. A basket of AUD 250,000 applies, and only the excess is recoverable (deductible basket).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 5,000 to 10,000 and a tipping basket of about 0.5% of price (AUD 120,000), so that once exceeded, the claim is recovered from the first dollar. Specific indemnities and fundamental warranties are excluded from both thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Convert to a tipping basket and reduce the de minimis, because a deductible basket of AUD 250,000 would absorb the entire AUD 180,000 Ironquay exposure.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general claims, with the same limit applied to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 36 months for general warranties. Fundamental warranties and title: 6 years, aligned with the NSW contract limitation period (confirm under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW)). Tax: statute of limitations plus 60 days.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a single period for all claims. Category-specific periods are needed because the 18-month window closes before many tax and privacy exposures crystallise.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share ownership) capped at 100% of price, with the 6-year period above, and outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title failure is a binary, high-value risk, and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap it at AUD 4.8m.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8, and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud, dishonesty, and wilful concealment are excluded from all caps, time limits, thresholds, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions. Australian law generally will not allow a party to contract out of its own fraud, but the carve-out should be express.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out. The current drafting could be read to cover fraud, which is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 deem every fact in the data room (through 5.00pm 22 September 2026) and all public registers and accounts as disclosed.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with a fair-disclosure standard. No deemed disclosure of the data room or public records.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. General data room disclosure would hollow out the warranties entirely.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. Add an express pro-sandbagging clause so that the buyer's knowledge does not defeat a warranty claim. Known matters that are material should be handled through specific indemnities or price adjustments, not left to the warranty regime.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3 and insert a pro-sandbagging clause. Clause 8.3 combined with 1.1 would mean the buyer carries every known issue listed in this review.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30%) consent is "addressed." The seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the condition as satisfied on delivery of counterparty written consent. The final consent and 11.3 conditions are not in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Written Bluefen consent in agreed form, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. A buyer termination right if not received. A specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue within a set period after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a hard condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation. Concentration risk of this size cannot be left to a warranty claim.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release to be provided after Completion. Not repaid, and no final discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price (debt-free basis), with a payoff letter, and discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations and any guarantees) delivered at Completion or held in escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. The buyer should not fund a secured lender while the security remains in place.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are absent from the funds flow. Payroll tax and superannuation treatment is not stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Treated as a debt-like item or seller transaction cost, deducted from price. Seller to bear all associated payroll tax (NSW), superannuation, and on-costs, backed by a specific uncapped indemnity. A corrected funds flow before signing.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct AUD 420,000 plus on-costs from price. Under a debt-free, cash-free deal, Completion-triggered payments are the seller's responsibility.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay arrangement conditions transfer of project materials on payment. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank-verified, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Evidence of payment or payment at Completion as a debt-like item. A confirmatory assignment of all SOW3 project materials as a condition precedent. An indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, third-party IP infringement claims, and ownership of project materials, outside thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." A narrow indemnity limited to a single payment leaves ownership of the core IP unprotected.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 export (possibly about 1,240 records: names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. Investigation is preliminary, and the seller says it is "not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of an independent forensic investigation before signing. An assessment of whether the Company is an APP entity and whether an eligible data breach has occurred under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), including any OAIC and individual notification obligations. A specific indemnity covering notification, remediation, regulatory, and third-party costs, outside thresholds and with a longer survival period. Consider an escrow or holdback.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not expected to be material." The seller has not established the scope, and the investigation should precede signing.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs." DD-008 and DD-011 do not state whether they are terminable, unavoidable, or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Full contract terms and renewal history. Renewals entered outside the ordinary course, or commitments extending beyond Completion that are not reflected in the price, treated as a price adjustment or seller cost. A warranty that no commitments were entered outside the ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm the terms before accepting "ordinary course." Treat any amount that is not ordinary-course and not reflected in working capital as a price adjustment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All claims, including fundamental, tax, and specific matters, are placed under one regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental warranties, (c) tax, (d) IP, (e) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, Sandbar), and (f) fraud. Each with its own cap, period, and threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single-regime approach. Different risks carry different values and time horizons.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, which shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of shares. The seller does not confirm that the buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register and share certificates, verification of the transfer form, PPSR and other encumbrance searches, and confirmation that no options or convertible instruments exist. A title warranty plus an indemnity under the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent title verification before signing. The register is the seller's own document and is not proof of unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." The draft excerpt contains no detailed tax or IP warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Full tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, uncapped up to price, with the extended period in SPA-N-003. Specific IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, open-source use, and employee and contractor IP assignment. Specific indemnities for pre-Completion payroll tax and the bonuses.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." Tax and IP require their own warranties and indemnities.

---

**Next steps:**
1. Confirm with the deal team whether any principal-level agreement exists, and treat the "FINAL" label as a negotiating position.
2. Commission forensic review (SPA-N-012), title verification (SPA-N-015), and Ironquay payment evidence (SPA-N-011) before signing.
3. Require a corrected funds flow that includes the Riverlark payout, bonuses, and any other debt-like items.
4. Have NSW-qualified counsel verify the statutory references (Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, NSW payroll tax) and the enforceability of each proposed position before mark-up.
